contentCheck.notes: Two full pages show parts (a)-(d)(iv), the reaction equations, and the [O3] vs time graph; crops equal the page contexts.

primary.evidence: Must draw the O3 Lewis diagram, placing 18 valence electrons with one double bond and lone pairs on the central O.
Explicitly requires all valid resonance structures, i.e. both placements of the O=O double bond.
Asks for the shape of O3 based on the drawn Lewis structure.

supporting.evidence: Must count three electron domains on the central O, including one lone pair, to determine the shape.

primary.evidence: Must use bonds broken minus bonds formed with the given O2 bond enthalpy and reaction enthalpy to solve for the average O-O bond enthalpy in O3, counting two O-O bonds per O3.
Must read the time for [O3] to fall from 1.0e-5 to 5.0e-6 M on the graph to obtain the first-order half-life.
Must use the first-order relation k = 0.693/t1/2 with the half-life to get k1 in s^-1.
Must explain that because [HSO3-] is in large excess and stays essentially constant, the second-order rate law reduces to an apparent first-order dependence on [O3].
Must propose varying the initial [HSO3-] while monitoring the rate (or observed k) to show first-order dependence on HSO3-.
